Liubeshiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Liubeshiv's Jews are first mentioned during the Khmelnytsky uprising, which some survived; the population expanded rapidly from 831 in 1847 to about 1,800 by 1886, served across generations by rabbis of the Weingarten family. During WWI, all but one family were deported to Poland; by 1936, around 1,500 Jews had returned. An attempted pogrom during the interwar period was fought off by local self-defense organizations. A ghetto established in May 1942 held about 2,000 Jews; most were murdered during its August 15, 1942 liquidation, with the remainder executed that November. After the war, the Liubeshiv Jews shot in August 1942 were reburied in this cemetery, which may be the town's new cemetery, though the location of an older one is unknown.
